messages.subject: Question - Phylogenetic Tree Chap 8
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I am using the wondefull book about "Data Integration, Manipulation and Visualization of Phylogenetic Trees" https://yulab-smu.github.io/treedata-book/index.html and I have a question about your guide at "Chapter 8 Annotating Tree with Silhouette Images and Sub-plots".

I use the source code as below and I have two problems :

1) I do not understand what to do with to fix the function 'full_join'

> tree2 <- full_join(tree, data.frame(label = names(x), stat = x ), by = 'label')
Error in UseMethod("full_join") :
  no applicable method for 'full_join' applied to an object of class "c('simmap', 'phylo')"

2) Why RStudio did not find the function geom_inset while I loaded (I think) the suitable libraries ?

> ?geom_inset
No documentation for ‘geom_inset’ in specified packages and libraries:
you could try ‘??geom_inset’

###This is the code
library(phytools)
library(ape)
library(ggplot2)
library(tibble)
library(phytools)
library(ggtree)
library(treeio)
library(ggimage)

data(anoletree)
x <- getStates(anoletree,"tips")
tree <- anoletree

cols <- setNames(palette()[1:length(unique(x))],sort(unique(x)))
fitER <- ape::ace(x,tree,model="ER",type="discrete")
ancstats <- as.data.frame(fitER$lik.anc)
ancstats$node <- 1:tree$Nnode+Ntip(tree)

## cols parameter indicate which columns store stats
bars <- nodebar(ancstats, cols=1:6)
bars <- lapply(bars, function(g) g+scale_fill_manual(values = cols))

tree2 <- ggtree:full_join(tree, data.frame(label = names(x), stat = x ), by = 'label')
p <- ggtree(tree2) + geom_tiplab() +
  geom_tippoint(aes(color = stat)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = cols) +
  theme(legend.position = "right") +
  xlim(NA, 8)
p + geom_inset(bars, width = .08, height = .05, x = "branch")

Thanks you for helping,

Kinds regards,

Grégoire

messages.subject: Could geom_inset place image of different size on branch?
messages.subject_clean: Could geom_inset place image of different size on branch?
messages.body_plain:
Prof. Yu:
      Thanks for the development of ggtree. Recently I have been trying to visualising evolutionary events on phylogenetic tree using ggtree. I combined nodebar function and  geom_inset function under the instruction of ggtree book attempting to visualise the number of two evolutionary events. Here is my code

bar2<-nodebar(barstat,cols=(1:2),position="dodge")
bar2<-lapply(bar2, function(g) g+scale_fill_manual(values=c('#817e5f','#d73635')))
p + geom_inset(bar2,width=.09,height=.08,x = "branch",vjust=.1)

And I got the following graph. It seems that the geom_inset function puts every image of same size as specified by width and height on the branch? This hampers the visualisation of  number of events denoted by red bar. The height of red bars appears the same while in reality it should not be. Is there a workaround or solution in ggtree that could help me realise this?

Best regards
Ramon

You can open an issue to request aes mapping for geom_inset.

messages.subject: geom_hilight in reversed x-axis
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am creating a plot with two phylogenetic trees with connected tips (Fig.3 attached) and I am having problems highlighting the clades of interest in the reversed x-axis. The geom_hilight works fine for the individual trees (Fig. 1 and 2 attached), but I not managing to make it work when the axis is reversed. Does anyone knows how to solve this problem?

Another problem I'm having is that when I add the tip labels in the final plot (with trees face to face and connecting lines) the plot gets messy because the labels are behind the lines. Is there any way to make the lines start in the end of the tip labels instead of by the branch?

Here is a piece of the code I am working with:

p1 <- ggtree(x_2) + ggtitle("ML") + theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.25)) +
      geom_hilight(node=113, fill="steelblue", alpha=.6) +
      geom_hilight(node=116, fill="yellow", alpha=.6) +
      geom_hilight(node=154, fill="green", alpha=.6)

p2 <- ggtree(y_2) + ggtitle("BI") + theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.25)) +
      geom_hilight(node=190, fill="steelblue", alpha=.6) +
      geom_hilight(node=112, fill="yellow", alpha=.6) +
      geom_hilight(node=142, fill="green", alpha=.6)

# create tibbles from $data
d1 <- p1$data
d2 <- p2$data

# reverse x-axis and set offset to make the tree in the right hand side of the first tree
d2$x <- max(d2$x) - d2$x + max(d1$x) + 1

pp <- p1 +  geom_tree(data=d2) + labs(title = "ML vs BI", caption="Programs used to generate the trees: RaxML and MrBayes")

dd <- bind_rows(d1, d2) %>%     # bind multiple data frames by row and column
      filter(!is.na <http://is.na>(label))                   # 'filter' return rows with matching conditions, in this case the 'labels' (tip labels)

pp + geom_line(aes(x, y, group=label), data=dd, color='grey')

Thank you!
Gustavo
